beats.say: Storm for storm, there's no sign Bay of Bengal cyclones are stronger.
beats.caption: Stronger? No sign, storm for storm

beats.say: India's weather service counts six in ten storms turning severe, in the Bay and the Arabian Sea.
beats.caption: IMD 1982–2024: 62% vs 62% turn severe

beats.say: But the Bay makes about twice as many cyclones, and the deadliest on record.
beats.caption: About 2× as many · deadliest on record

beats.say: In nineteen seventy, in what is now Bangladesh, at least three hundred thousand died, mostly from the storm surge.
beats.caption: 1970: 300,000+ died (WMO estimate)

beats.say: Why? At its head the Bay narrows like a funnel, with shallow water and crowded low islands.
beats.caption: The Bay narrows: 1,400 km → under 500 km

beats.say: So it's less about stronger storms, more about where they land.
beats.caption: Not stronger storms: where they land

beats.say: Stronger? No. Deadliest on record? Yes.
beats.caption: Stronger? No. Deadliest on record? Yes.

title: Why the Bay of Bengal makes the deadliest cyclones
